title: The Dev Guild's Regenerative Stack
dek: How the Greenpill Dev Guild plans to fund regenerative work, from squad staking to Green Goods, in its own posts on Paragraph.
excerpt: The Dev Guild's four-layer stack links validator rewards, allocation tools, reputation and impact reporting into one funding loop.
body:
Since it began in October 2023, the Greenpill Dev Guild has looked for ways to fund regenerative work from the impact it creates, rather than from one grant after another. Between June 30 and July 6, 2025, the guild published a seven-part series on Paragraph, Pioneering a Regenerative Stack, describing its answer as four connected layers of the Ethereum ecosystem.

## Four layers

- Blockchain: squad staking, where a small group stakes 32 ETH together with tools from Obol, Dappnode and Lido, so validator rewards can fund public goods.
- Protocol: the Allo Alliance, where builders work on allocation tools such as Grant Ships, conviction voting, streaming funds and cookie jars.
- Social: GreenWill, a reputation tool that turns regenerative actions into a verifiable record for governance.
- Application: Green Goods, an app that makes grassroots conservation work visible, verifiable and fundable.

The series closed with Capital Formation, on how verified impact data could connect the stack to larger pools of funding, and Validating the Regenerative Stack, a roadmap for pilots in the second half of 2025.

## The Public Goods Staking Protocol

On March 23, 2026, the guild published The Public Goods Staking Protocol v0. In it, small squads use distributed validator technology to run Ethereum validators together and send the yield to Octant vaults, which keep the principal separate so only the yield is spent. The protocol builds on Dappnode, Obol DVT, the Lido Community Staking Module and Octant Vaults. With a 2.4 ETH bond, a squad can access 32 ETH of delegated capital to run a validator.
